title: introduce-cost-drift-detector-and-one-click-profile-rollback
author: Devon Liu
description: Motivation: tenant cost profiles can drift over time as workload shape or token mix changes. Teams currently surfacing regressions requires manual investigation (cost dashboards + rollbacks) which is slow during incidents. This PR adds a low-risk, observable automation that: 1) continuously monitors unit-econ signals (tokens-per-request, avg latency, cache hit rate, batch shapes) and emits a drift alert when a tenant's observed execution cost deviates from its pinned profile by configurable thresholds; 2) surfaces a one-click rollback in the Console to revert to the last known-good cost profile (batch/cache/quant presets) with an audit log and optional dry-run. Key goals: reduce MTTR for cost regressions, provide safe manual rollback, and collect labeled drift examples for future auto-suggests. Changeset overview: - runtime/prefill/cost_drift_detector.go: new detector that ingests aggregated metrics, computes per-tenant expected vs observed unit-cost delta, and produces drift events with severity scoring. Implements exponential smoothing for short-term noise rejection and a configurable cooldown window. - telemetry/cost_drift_metrics.yaml: new metrics & alerts (cost_drift_score, cost_drift_severity, rollback_events). - console/src/components/CostProfileRollbackButton.tsx: UI button that opens a rollback confirmation modal showing diff between active and candidate profiles and estimated unit-cost impact. - console/src/routes/cost-ops.ts: backend endpoint for initiating rollback, performs validation and writes audit entry. - pkg/econ/profile_store.go: profile snapshot + versioning helpers; added soft-lock support to avoid concurrent rollbacks. - docs/runbooks/cost-drift.md: runbook describing investigation steps and rollback guidance. - tests/integration/cost_drift_detector_test.go: deterministic integration tests simulating spike/drift scenarios and validating alarms + rollback safety checks. Rollout plan: feature gated behind tenant opt-in flag (runtime feature flag: enable_cost_drift_detector). Will deploy as opt-in to 5 pilot tenants for 2 weeks before wider enablement. Safety: rollbacks are manual (one-click) not automatic. Audit log captures user id, snapshot id, and pre/post profile. The detector uses conservative thresholds by default (10% unit-econ delta sustained for 30m) and exposes tuning knobs per-tenant. Checklist: - [x] Detector algorithm implemented and unit/integration tested - [x] Console UI implemented and E2E smoke-tested locally - [x] Telemetry & alert definitions added - [x] Runbook drafted - [x] Feature gated behind runtime flag and hidden by default - [x] Security review (audit log & RBAC) performed Notable implementation details: - We compute a weighted unit-cost delta combining token-cost and GPU-time proxies to avoid noisy single-metric triggers. - The detector stores short-lived state in the tiered cache (in-memory + Redis) to keep evaluation latency <50ms. - Rollback endpoint validates compatibility between active profile and candidate snapshot; incompatible snapshots return 409 with a suggested migration plan. Related: ENG-1942 (cost incident postmortem), ENG-1988 (profile versioning work).

review_comments: Aisha Morgan: Nice work—algorithm reads well. Please add a short test for extremely noisy tenants so we don't flip on short bursts.
Devon Liu: Added noisy-tenant test in second commit (b3d9e21).
Rafael Ortega: Question on DB soft-locks: what happens if a rollback fails halfway? Please ensure idempotency.
Devon Liu: rollback endpoint runs inside a DB tx and writes a rollback_event marker; failure will leave profile untouched and surface a 500 with guidance.

ci_summary: Initial CI surfaced a flaky e2e (console modal snapshot) which was fixed by stabilizing the test timing. All checks green on re-run (unit/integration/e2e/lint).
release_notes: Add cost-drift detector (opt-in) and one-click profile rollback in Console. Feature is behind feature-flag and available to pilot tenants only. See runbook for operational guidance.
post_merge_actions: 1) Enable feature flag for pilot tenants via infra flagger. 2) Run canary on two low-traffic tenants for 48h. 3) Add drift events to incident playbook. 4) Schedule follow-up to collect labeled drift traces for auto-suggest heuristics.
qa_notes: Integration tests simulate sustained token-cost deltas and verify that drift events are emitted and rollback validation prevents incompatible snapshots. Manual QA: exercised console rollback flow against a staging tenant snapshot. Observed audit log entries with requestor metadata.
risk_assessment: Low-medium: detector itself is read-only; surface actions are manual. Primary risk is noisy alerts — mitigated with conservative defaults and smoothing. Rollbacks are transactional and audited.
authors_reply_to_review: Thanks for the feedback—addressed noisy-tenant test, added delta estimate to modal, and made rollback idempotent with a DB marker. Will follow up with a subsequent PR to expose per-tenant threshold overrides in the Console.
notes: This PR intentionally avoids automatic rollbacks; we want labeled human confirmations first to build a small corpus of true positives/negatives before attempting automated remediation.
